speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I can see you are experiencing jaundice and agitation, which suggests we need to investigate your liver function immediately. When did these symptoms first appear, and have you noticed any changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To help narrow down the cause of your jaundice and agitation, have you experienced any right upper quadrant abdominal pain, fever, or nausea? Also, have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your high-risk sexual history and the combination of jaundice with agitation, I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis, particularly Hepatitis A or B. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_A_IgM, Hepatitis_B_surface_antigen, Liver_Function_Panel, INR

text: The positive Hepatitis A IgM and significantly elevated liver enzymes confirm acute Hepatitis A infection. The agitation and coagulopathy suggest severe disease, so I am requesting imaging to assess liver status. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of acute jaundice, agitation, and coagulopathy in the setting of a positive Hepatitis A IgM test confirms severe acute viral hepatitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis A with fulminant hepatic failure
